problem_statement:
k_sleep() returns incorrect remaining time after approximately 12 days of continuous uptime (or sooner depending on tick frequency). The issue manifests when the 32-bit kernel tick counter wraps around.

When a thread calls k_sleep() with a timeout and is woken early by k_wakeup(), the return value should indicate the remaining sleep time. However, after the 32-bit tick counter wraps (2^32 ticks), the return value becomes corrupted — it may return 0 instead of the correct remaining time.

The root cause is in z_tick_sleep() in kernel/sched.c. The calculation:

  ticks = (k_ticks_t)expected_wakeup_ticks - sys_clock_tick_get_32();

fails because both expected_wakeup_ticks and sys_clock_tick_get_32() are uint32_t values that may independently wrap. When one wraps but the other hasn't, the subtraction result (a uint32_t) is then cast to k_ticks_t (which may be 64-bit), producing a corrupted value.

The calculation must be performed using 32-bit unsigned integer semantics to handle wraparound properly before any widening conversion.

Reproduction timing depends on tick frequency:
  - 4096 ticks/sec (production LSE): ~12 days
  - 50000 ticks/sec (Cortex-M Systick): ~24 hours
  - 100 Hz test tick: ~497 days (but can be forced by setting the tick counter)

See: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/79863
